intervals.label: observations
intervals.note: The first (30/40 GHz) receiver started observing in early 2020 (also "since 2020", LAMBDA); further receivers were added later. The official BICEP/Keck publication list (checked 2026-10-26) includes a 2026 SPIE paper titled "Optical characterization of the BICEP Array 150 and 220/270 GHz CMB polarimeters in the 2026 season".
intervals.quote: The 30/40 GHz receiver is designed to constrain the synchrotron foreground and has begun observing at the South Pole in early 2020.

placements.note: Replaces the Keck Array on its South Pole mount; the sources do not give a more precise location than the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station.
placements.quote: For the past decade, the BICEP/Keck collaboration has been operating a series of telescopes at the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station

diameter.quote: It is comprised of four 550 mm aperture refractive telescopes

sensor_count.note: Design figure for the full four-receiver instrument ("over 30,000 detectors"); not all receivers may be deployed.

telescope_count.quote: It is comprised of four 550 mm aperture refractive telescopes

summary.plain: The newest BICEP/Keck instrument: four 55-centimetre refracting telescopes covering six frequency bands from 30 to 270 GHz, built to separate galactic dust and synchrotron from a possible inflationary signal.
summary.technical: Four BICEP3-class receivers (550 mm aperture) at 30/40, 95, 150 and 220/270 GHz with over 30,000 detectors at the South Pole; first receiver observing since early 2020; replaced the Keck Array.

technology.quote: It is comprised of four 550 mm aperture refractive telescopes observing the polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) at 30/40, 95, 150 and 220/270 GHz with over 30,000 detectors.
technology.value: Four 550 mm aperture refracting telescopes (receivers) observing CMB polarization at 30/40, 95, 150 and 220/270 GHz.
